headline: Measles in an Immunized School-Aged Population -- New Mexico
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: From February 10 to April 15, 1984, 76 measles cases were reported in Hobbs, New Mexico, where the school system said 98% of students had been vaccinated before the outbreak began.

headline: Epidemiologic Notes and Reports Measles Transmitted in a Medical Office Building -- New Mexico, 1986
source: CDC, Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report
blurb: In January 1986, New Mexico health officials identified 24 measles patients after a Santa Fe pediatrician reported three suspected cases, and nine of the patients had visited the same medical offices on one day.

headline: EXEMPTION FROM SCHOOL, CHILDCARE, AND PRE-SCHOOL IMMUNIZATION
blurb: This New Mexico rule, in effect since November 27, 2013, sets out how families can ask for a medical or religious exemption from the immunizations required for school and child care.

headline: Whooping cough cases in New Mexico nearly double this year
blurb: New Mexico's health department said the state had 60 whooping cough cases as of October 26, 2024, almost double the number from the year before.

headline: Measles outbreak declared in Lea County
blurb: New Mexico's health department declared a measles outbreak after three cases were confirmed in one week in Lea County, which borders Gaines County, Texas.

headline: Lea County resident tests positive for measles after death
blurb: New Mexico's health department confirmed that an unvaccinated Lea County resident who died had tested positive for measles, and said the cause of death was still under investigation.

headline: New Mexico Health Department calls end of measles outbreak
blurb: New Mexico declared its measles outbreak over after 42 days with no new cases, with 100 cases counted in what the state called its first measles outbreak since 1996.
